question: On 27 March 2026, the Commission issued C(2026)1964, terminating the procedure for authorising lithium orotate dihydrate (NF/2024/30250) as a novel food, without updating the Union list. The specific justification for this has not been published on the Commission’s website.

The information available to us suggests that the procedure was not terminated on the basis of a final scientific assessment, but because the application did not contain the full information requested as regards the identity of the novel food, the production process, the exact composition of the novel food and the scientific evidence demonstrating its safety. In 2025, Aron et al.

reported in ‘Lithium deficiency and the onset of Alzheimer’s disease’, Nature 645, 712-721, that lithium homeostasis is already disrupted in the human brain in cases of mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer’s. Experimental lithium deficiency exacerbated pathology and cognitive deficits in mouse models of Alzheimer’s disease; low‑dose lithium orotate prevented or reduced several of these changes. 1.
What specific information regarding identity, the production process, composition and safety was deemed to be missing or insufficient?
What were the scientific safety concerns – if any – about lithium orotate dihydrate, irrespective of any lack of completeness from a formal or documentation-related point of view?

Was the Nature paper by Aron et al. (‘Lithium deficiency and the onset of Alzheimer’s disease’) taken into account? If not, is the Commission or EFSA intending to take it into account if the application is resubmitted, in particular the effects of very low doses of lithium orotate in the Alzheimer’s mouse model that are reported in the paper?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.10.

2026) The Commission adopted the decision terminating the procedure for authorising the placing on the market of lithium orotate dihydrate as a novel food, on the ground that the application was not valid pursuant to Article 6 of Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/24691 because the applicant did not provide all the information required in Article 10(2) of Regulation (EU) 2015/22832 and Articles 3 and 5 of Regulation (EU) 2017/2469.

Regarding identity, the applicant had not provided sufficient information to identify and characterise the novel food, such as data on physicochemical properties and analytical confirmation of the identity of lithium orotate dihydrate.

The description of the production process lacked details on the chemical reaction, synthesis of the novel food, purification steps, reagents used and their ratios, and quality controls measures. Compositional data were also incomplete such as on batch-to-batch variability and stability, presence of small particles (including nanoscale particles).

Supporting evidence, such as certificates of analysis, accreditations, and method validation reports, was missing. Regarding safety, the application lacked toxicological studies (e.g., genotoxicity and 90-day subchronic toxicity), an allergenicity assessment, and data on absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion (ADME).

As the application was not considered valid by the Commission, the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) didn’t carry out a safety risk assessment of lithium orotate dihydrate, and no conclusions on the safety or not of this novel food could be reached. The paper by Aron et al.

(Nature, 2025) was not taken into account since the application did not reach the stage in which EFSA would carry out a safety scientific risk assessment. Should a new application be submitted and the Commission would consider it valid, EFSA would carry out a full safety risk assessment taking into account all the relevant scientific evidence available.
1 Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/2469 of 20 December 2017 laying down administrative and
scientific requirements for applications referred to in Article 10 of Regulation (EU) 2015/2283 of the European Parliament and of the Council on novel foods. OJ L 351, 30.12.2017, p. 64.

2 Regulation (EU) 2015/2283 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2015 on novel foods, amending Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 of the European Parliament and of the Council and repealing Regulation (EC) No 258/97 of the European Parliament and of the Council and Commission Regulation (EC) No 1852/2001. OJ L 327, 11.12.2015, p. 1.
